history.summary: FLAG - IDENTITY AMBIGUITY: the CSV row 'Suryakund Temple' most plausibly refers to the Surya Kund within the Surajkund hot-spring complex in Belkapi gram panchayat, Barkatha block, Hazaribagh district - a natural geothermal site rather than a single built temple. The complex has five kunds: Surya Kund, Lakshman Kund, Brahm Kund, Ram Kund and Sita Kund. It is claimed to be the hottest natural spring in India (surface temperature ~87 C / 189 F, subsurface ~165 C), with sulphur-rich water reputed to have healing properties. Local legend and Hindu scriptures (per travel sites) treat it as a sacred site visited by sages; archaeological claims of Gupta-era use are unverified. A Durga temple has been constructed near the springs in more recent years (per Alchetron/Wikipedia). Justdial lists 'Surajkund Dhaam' at Surujkhurd Belkapi (4.2/585 ratings). FLAG - TOWN CORRECTED: CSV town 'Hazaribag' is approximate; the site is ~72 km from Hazaribagh town and 5 km from Barkatha on the Grand Trunk Road (NH 19); town field corrected to Barkatha (nearest town). Coordinates corroborated across sources (Wikipedia/Alchetron 24.1494N 85.6456E; geocoder 24.15428N 85.64737E).
